The Cougars, led by second-year head coach [[Brian Barone]], played their home games in the [[Vadalabene Center|First Community Arena at Vadalabene Center]] in [[Edwardsville, Illinois]] as members of the [[Ohio Valley Conference]].{{cite web|url=http://ovcsports.com/sports/2012/6/14/GEN_0614121029.aspx |title=OVC Member Institutions |publisher=Ohio Valley Conference |accessdate=21 October 2020 }} == Previous season == The [[2019–20 SIU Edwardsville Cougars men's basketball team|Cougars]] finished the [[2019–20 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2019–20 season]] 8–23, 5–13 in [[2019–20 Ohio Valley Conference men's basketball season|OVC play]] to finish in a tie for tenth place. The Cougars failed to qualify for the OVC Tournament. == Preseason == Five players who saw major playing time and a third-year former [[Walk-on (sports)|walk-on]] return from the 8–23 team of 2019–20. They are joined by one junior who saw considerable action in the 2018-19 season but sat out last season as a medical [[Redshirt (college sports)|"redshirt"]], three freshmen, three junior college transfers, and one transfer from another Division I program. Coach Barone, his assistants, and the Cougars recruited probably the strongest incoming group in the program's history. The recruits included SIUE's first legitimate [[Blue chip (sports)|"blue chip"]] recruit, [[Ray'Sean Taylor]] from nearby [[Collinsville, Illinois|Collinsville]], who suffered an [[Anterior cruciate ligament|ACL]] injury that ended his first Cougars season before it began. A second :"blue chipper" came on board with Sidney Wilson's late transfer from [[UConn Huskies men's basketball|Connecticut]]. Three scholarship players with eligibility remaining did not return; two transferred to other Division I programs,{{cite web |url=https://uicflames.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/treavon-martin/7939 |title=2020-21 Men's Basketball Roster 25 Treavon Martin |publisher=University of Illinois at Chicago Athletics |accessdate= 4 December 2020 }}{{cite web |url=https://ncataggies.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/kenyon-duling/2768 |title=2020-21 Men's Basketball Roster 21 Kenyon Duling |publisher=North Carolina A&T State University |accessdate= 4 December 2020 }} and [[Zeke Moore (basketball)|Zeke Moore]] is playing professionally in Spain. In a vote of conference coaches and sports information directors, SIUE was picked to finish in 11th place in the OVC.{{cite web|url=http://ovcsports.com/news/2020/11/4/mens-basketball-media-poll-tabs-austin-peay-and-murray-state-men-ut-martin-women-as-2020-21-ovc-basketball-preseason-favorites.aspx |title=Media Poll Tabs Austin Peay and Murray State Men, UT Martin Women as 2020-21 OVC Basketball Preseason Favorites |publisher=Ohio Valley Conference|date=November 17, 2020|accessdate=18 December 2020 }} ==Regular season== After leading the team with career-highs of 18 points, 7 rebounds, and 5 assists in the Cougars' win at Morehead State, '''Sidney Wilson''' was named the ''OVC Newcomer of the Week'' on December 21.{{cite web |url=http://ovcsports.com/news/2020/12/21/ovc-mens-basketball-report-december-21.aspx |title=OVC Men's Basketball Report - December 21 |publisher= Ohio Valley Conference |date=December 21, 2020 |access-date=16 January 2021 }} The ongoing [[COVID-19 pandemic]] necessitated revision after revision to the Cougars' schedule. The game at [[2020-21 Northwestern Wildcats men's basketball team|Northwestern]] was cancelled, and nine (9) OVC games were postponed, including a postponement of a rescheduled game. After averaging 18.0 points, 4.3 rebounds, 2.3 assists and 1.3 blocks/game while hitting 50 percent (20-of-40) from the field and 73.3 percent (11-of-15) from the free throw line in three road games, '''Sydney Wilson''' was again named the ''OVC Newcomer of the Week'' on February 1.{{cite web |url=https://www.siuecougars.com/sports/m-baskbl/2020-21/releases/20210201lth3m4 |title=OVC Men's Basketball Report - - February 1 |publisher=Ohio Valley Conference |date=February 1, 2020 |access-date=1 February 2021 |archive-date=1 February 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210201193345/https://www.siuecougars.com/sports/m-baskbl/2020-21/releases/20210201lth3m4 |url-status=dead }} The Cougars went 33 days without a game in the span between December 18 and January 21, To make up for the nine game postponements, SIUE was scheduled to play four games per week. Then the OVC ruled that no more than three games were to be played per week; this change brought about a tenth postponement and the cancelation of a game versus Jacksonville State. COVID-19, injuries, and the wear and tear of too many games in too few days to make up for all of the postponements resulted in less success than hoped for. However, the Cougars qualified for th Ohio Valley Conference Tournament, after missing it last season. This was helped by the Cougars' six road wins, the most in the Division I era.{{cite web |url=https://www.siuecougars.com/sports/m-baskbl/2020-21/releases/20210225yontd7 |title=Men's Basketball Finds A Way to Return to Postseason |publisher=Southern Illinois University Edewardsville |date=February 25, 2020 |access-date=26 February 2021 }}{{Dead link|date=February 2022 |bot=InternetArchiveBot
